articles.headline: THE REFUGEES (3) buy a quarterback, and Parkers Dead Sons (7) rebuild at 0-4
articles.dek: Three completed deals inside forty-eight hours. The REFUGEES pay a 2027 third for Jameis Winston with Jaxson Dart ruled out; Dead Sons make two trades in two days after losing a game by 2.08.
body: THE REFUGEES have traded a 2027 third-round pick to Latina Lip-Pickers for Jameis Winston, closing a quarterback hole that opened when Jaxson Dart was ruled out with a knee injury.

It is a small price for a real problem. Dart is one of six players currently listed Out while sitting in somebody's starting lineup, and the REFUGEES were the only one of those teams without a ready replacement already rostered. Winston projects for 23.06 this week, which is not a headline number but is a functioning one, and the cost was a late pick two drafts away.

The REFUGEES are 4-0 and unbeaten in both columns, coming off the highest individual score in the league — Josh Allen's 51.22 on Sunday. Paying a third-rounder to avoid starting nobody at quarterback is the least dramatic move of the week and probably the most sensible.
The louder activity is at Parkers Dead Sons, who have made two trades in two days and are 0-4 in a way that flatters nobody.

On Monday, Dead Sons sent Courtland Sutton, their own 2028 first and a 2027 third to Gods Favorite Jew, and got Jadarian Price back. Later the same day they moved Dallas Goedert and Brian Robinson to Commercial Break for David Montgomery and Colston Loveland, sending four picks the other way.

Read together, those are the moves of a manager who has looked at an 0-4 record and concluded the problem is not the roster. It might not be. Dead Sons lost last week by 2.08, a margin Justin Herbert could have covered on his own had he not returned 8.7 against a projection of 27.0. They have scored 271.1 points, more than three teams above them in the standings, and have nothing to show for it.

What they gave up is worth a closer look than the player names suggest. Among the picks heading to Commercial Break is a 2027 third that originally belonged to Shake and Bake — currently the most valuable third-rounder in the league, since Shake and Bake project to the lowest season max points of anyone. The 2027 third that went to Gods Favorite Jew came via Muffin Toppers and projects near the back of the round. Dead Sons sent the good one away and the thin one away with it.

Whether David Montgomery is the answer is a separate question. He arrives having produced 3.4 points against a 25.5 projection in Week 2 — the single worst shortfall in the league — in a Commercial Break loss of 19.54. He projects for 20.8 this week. Commercial Break, also 0-4, come out of the two deals holding a 2028 first, a 2027 second, a 2028 third and a 2027 third, which is a great deal of future for a team with no present.

Gods Favorite Jew, 1-3, took the quiet side of it and came out ahead on paper: Courtland Sutton, a 2028 first and a 2027 third arrive for Jadarian Price alone. On a day when two teams were busy reshaping, that reads less like a rebuild than a toll collected from one.

Elsewhere the injury list is thicker than the trade wire. Caleb Williams, DJ Moore, Zay Flowers, Nico Collins, Brock Bowers and Kyler Murray are all listed Out while sitting in a starting lineup, spread across six different teams. Only one of those six has responded with a trade.
Ballots for Week 3 close Thursday at 8 PM Eastern. Nine of twelve are in.

articles.headline: Lip-Pickers (6) run down Ripple Effect (1), and five teams are undone by one man each
articles.dek: Davante Adams beat his projection by 22.9 in a game decided by 9.66. He was not the only player who settled a matchup on his own — five of the six losing teams had someone miss by more than they lost by.
body: The Ripple Effect went into Week 2 as the unanimous No. 1 in the power poll, holding every first-place vote in the league. They scored 188.68 points, the second-highest total of the round, and lost.
Latina Lip-Pickers put up 198.34 — the highest score in the league — and did most of the damage after everyone else had finished.

Going into Monday, Ripple Effect led 170.98 to 157.84. A 13.14-point cushion with one player left on each side, and the favourite had the safer name: Kyren Williams, a starting back in a normal workload, against a single wide receiver. Williams delivered, more or less, with 17.7. Ripple Effect also started Odell Beckham, who finished on nought.
Davante Adams finished on 40.5 against a projection of 17.6. That surplus alone is 22.9 points, more than double the eventual 9.66 margin. He did not contribute to the win so much as constitute it.

The more uncomfortable number for Ripple Effect is on their own sheet. Bijan Robinson was projected for 33.3 and returned 11.6. In a game lost by 9.66, that shortfall of 21.7 is the result twice over. Patrick Mahomes went for 36.38, Amon-Ra St. Brown for 35.7, Jonathan Taylor for 34.2 — three players over 34 points, a total that would have beaten ten of the other eleven teams, and one running back having a quiet afternoon was enough to undo all of it.

That pattern held across the league to a degree that is slightly unnerving. Five of the six losing teams had a single starter miss their projection by more than the margin of defeat. Saquon Barkley returned 3.5 of a projected 25.0 as The Phantom Troupe lost by 15.62. Justin Herbert managed 8.7 of a projected 27.0 while Parkers Dead Sons lost by 2.08. DJ Moore posted minus 0.1 against a projection of 16.9 as Chinese Sweatshop lost by 14.40. David Montgomery, projected for 25.5, gave Commercial Break 3.4 in a 19.54-point defeat.
In other words, almost nobody was beaten this week. They were each let down by one person, and the identity of that person is the entire difference between 1-1 and 0-2.

The exception is Beasty Boys, who lost to Muffin Toppers 187.86 to 166.76 without any one player betraying them. Jacory Croskey-Merritt was the worst of it at 13.5 under, still short of the 21.10 margin. They were simply beaten, which is the second week running that Beasty Boys have posted a respectable number and lost with it.

The one-man theme ran the other way too. Josh Allen scored 51.22, the highest in the league, 17.9 clear of projection, in a REFUGEES win of 15.62 — another result that reverses without one player. Kenneth Walker was only 5.1 over his number for The Tax, which sounds trivial until you notice they won by 2.08.

The median sat at 151.99. Six teams cleared it: Lip-Pickers, Ripple Effect, Muffin Toppers, THE REFUGEES, Beasty Boys and Phantom Troupe. The Tax won their head-to-head and still finished under it, which is the sort of week that looks fine in the standings and less fine in the points column. Gods Favorite Jew did the same in reverse, beating Chinese Sweatshop 125.46 to 111.06 in a game where the winner was still nowhere near the median.

Ballots for Week 3 open Tuesday at midnight. The unanimous No. 1 has just been beaten by the team ranked sixth, and the question for twelve voters is whether that was a result or a running back having a bad Sunday.

articles.headline: Chinese Sweatshop (9) and Gods Favorite Jew (11) close Week 2 with the two lowest scores
articles.dek: Chinese Sweatshop (9) sit on 67.88. Gods Favorite Jew (11) sit on 100.26. Nobody else in the league is within eleven points of either of them.
body: Of the twelve scores posted in Week 2, the two smallest belong to the same matchup. Chinese Sweatshop have 67.88 points. Gods Favorite Jew have 100.26. The next worst in the league is Commercial Break on 111.96 — clear of Gods Favorite Jew by 11.7 and of Chinese Sweatshop by 44.08.
They play each other tonight, which is the only reason one of them is getting a win out of it.

Chinese Sweatshop trail by 32.38 and have two starters yet to register a point: Matthew Stafford and Isaiah Likely. That is the entire comeback. Applying the league's scoring to what is left, the projection has them finishing around 110.3 — Stafford for 26 and Likely for 16.4 — and that is the optimistic reading.

Because Gods Favorite Jew are still adding. Cam Skattebo and Blake Corum are yet to score, worth a projected 37.8 between them, which puts the other side somewhere near 138. The 32.38 is not a fixed target so much as a suggestion. Sweatshop need to outscore two players with two players, having already been outscored by a distance, and the maths gives them a 13 percent chance of managing it.

How Sweatshop got here is its own small catastrophe. DJ Moore finished on minus 0.1. Jayden Reed managed 0.9. DK Metcalf, the kind of name you start without thinking about it, returned 5.7. Tyler Shough's 28.38 is the only score on the sheet that would look normal on anyone else's team, and it is currently carrying 42 percent of the entire roster's output.

Gods Favorite Jew have the opposite problem, which is to say they have two good players and not much else. Brock Purdy's 36.08 and Geno Smith's 20.58 account for more than half their total. Bryce Lance contributed 1.3. It is not a performance anyone is putting on a highlight reel, but it has been enough to sit 32 points clear all weekend.
Neither side is going to trouble the league median of 151.06, so this is a straight fight over one win between two teams who are already looking up at everyone.

The poll, for what it is worth, sees no great difference between them either. Chinese Sweatshop (9) and Gods Favorite Jew (11) are separated by fifteen points and one spot in the standings, and both were ranked below Parkers Dead Sons (7), who are 0-2. A win tonight does not fix much. Losing it, on the other hand, would be the second-lowest score in the league losing to the third-lowest.
Monday night football, and the league will be watching for the wrong reasons.
